get.description: What Maku downloads to work with, and whether each is ready.

post.description: Starts downloading a tool, unless it's ready or already on its way.
Adds a folder to the library. Nothing in it changes; the next scan looks inside.

delete.description:
Takes a folder out of the library. Its files stay exactly where they are. Not while a
file in it is converting, or made and waiting for another app to let go of its original:
its result is about to take the original's place.

get.description: The library in a few numbers, for Home.

post.description: Starts scanning every library folder. Nothing in them changes.
Stops the scan after the file it's on; resuming carries on from there.

put.description:
Keeps the owner's choices. Turning the reports off takes them out of the video folders at
once; turning them on writes them again. So with the pictures next to each show: off, the
ones Maku wrote go at once; on, Maku's care writes them now.

post.description:
Checks this PC again and times each part, in the background (about a minute); unless a
check is under way already.

get.description: Whether Maku has a TMDB key, for episode lists, titles and artwork.

put.description:
Checks the key with TMDB, then keeps it on this PC. The videos waiting for it are then
looked up, at a scan; in Setup none has been read yet, so none starts.

delete.description: Forgets the key. Titles Maku already looked up stay.

Keeps the owner's choice of poster, or goes back to the one found. The poster next to the
show follows, when the owner has those.

get.description:
A picture from TMDB's image server, such as a guess's poster, fetched once and kept. Any
other address is refused.
A video in the library, in full.
One of a title's episodes as TMDB lists it, and its video when the library has it.

A picture for the top of a video's details: TMDB's from its episode, a frame from the
file, or its show's wide picture. Fetched or taken once, then kept. `Maku-Picture` says
which: `episode` or `show`.

put.description: Where a video is: the player says so as it plays, and as it stops.

post.description: Videos marked watched, or not watched: either way each starts from the top next time.

get.description: The titles to go on with, the latest played first: Home's "Continue watching".

delete.description: A title out of "Continue watching" till one of its videos plays again.

get.description:
Each of the library's titles with an episode airing today or later that the library hasn't
got: its next one, the soonest first.
How the health check stands, and the videos that didn't play.

post.description: Every video is played again, from tonight.
Test-plays one video now, as the night's check does.
The owner played it and it's fine: off the list, till next month's check.
The owner says it's broken: from now on it's a broken file, the check saying why.

get.description: The posters TMDB has of a title, to choose from (with the owner's key).

The library's series and films by any name they go by, their episodes by code or name,
and its videos by their files' names: what every word of `q` finds, however it's written.

Every file Maku couldn't place surely, folder by folder. With `title`, that title's files
as one, to change its match: its first file, with the others alike.

(or, with `title`, every file of that title). An episode Maku can't place is 422: the owner

get.description: One of three stills from the file (0, 1 or 2: 15%, 50% and 80% of the way in).

delete.description:
A series or film after all: the file waits for a match again, and the next scan looks it
up afresh.

get.description:
The files the owner said aren't a series or film, in name order: left where they are,
out of the library, each to match after all or delete.

parameters.description: Copies to keep over the others of an episode

post.description:
Makes the changes the owner reviewed, journaled so History can undo them, and puts the
English asked for from other copies in the queue. None is made when Maku proposes any of
them differently now.

Deletes videos the way Maku deletes: into the quarantine on their own drive, with their
subtitles, journaled so History can put them back till the quarantine is cleared out.

get.description:
What Maku did on its latest days with anything on them (a week's worth), newest first:
each tidy-up applied, each conversion, each batch of subtitles made and each scan.
`before` ("2026-10-07", the page's `older`) asks for the days before that one, and `q` for
what names a series, a film or a file ("Starfall 03"), on the days it finds anything on.

post.description:
Forgets what Maku did before the last day, week or month, or all of it. What still has a
copy in quarantine stays, so it can be put back, and nothing on disk changes.

Puts back what a tidy-up moved, or what couldn't go back last time. For a conversion,
the original comes back in the converted file's place.

Opens a video to play: a ticket for its stream, with its sound, subtitles and chapters.
A video whose drive isn't connected, or that went, has no ticket, and says which.

get.description: How the open video's subtitles are getting on, and why its stream stopped if it did.

delete.description: Closes the video: its stream stops, and so does any copy of its subtitles.

post.description:
Gets subtitles ready to draw in: text in the file is copied out of it first, which reads
the whole file.

get.description:
Every video not at the standard yet, with what it gets, and what that takes on this
PC.

One side of the comparison: a frame of the file as it is (`before`), or as converting
makes it (`after`), taken at one of three points (0, 1 or 2: 15%, 50% and 80% of the way
in).

post.description: Puts files at the end of the queue, to convert now, at night, or after what waits.
Stops the file converting now (it starts over on resuming) and takes no other.

On a drive without room for all that waits on it, the files that fit convert, and the
rest wait for room while the others go. The queue goes on if it paused.

Deletes everything set aside on a drive now, however recently, to make room there: it
can't be put back after. Maku asks the owner first. Files waiting for room look again.

put.description: Converts whenever files wait, or only at night (23:00 to 07:00).

On the nights-only schedule: tonight's run stops taking files at 03:00, so Windows' sleep
comes back sooner, or goes on till 07:00.

post.description: Takes several waiting files out of the queue; one no longer waiting is passed over.
Puts several waiting files together before another, or last, in the order they wait in.

Cancels everything: every file waiting leaves the queue, and the one converting stops. The
files themselves stay as they are.
Passes over a file: the one converting stops, one waiting leaves the line.

Marks a file whose conversion failed as broken: the library counts it among the files
that won't play, and it isn't converted again till it changes.

A failed or skipped file goes back in the queue, last; one made and waiting for another
app to let go of its original is tried again now ("Try now"). Subtitles go at `quality`
when it's given: Fast, after the card ran out of memory for Best ("Make them with Fast").
Puts a converted file's original back in its place, from quarantine.

get.description:
The library's videos that have sound, with what they can be heard and read in: what
Maku could make English subtitles for, and how long that takes.

post.description:
Puts videos in the queue for English subtitles, as one batch, to make now, at night, or
after what waits. A video waiting for them already, or one without sound, is passed over.

Sets aside the subtitles a batch made that are there as Maku wrote them, to the
quarantine, as a tidy-up History can undo.

get.description: How big each part of Maku's data is, and the quarantine on each drive.

post.description:
Moves Maku's data to another folder as the engine starts again: the app starts it again
right after asking.

Writes the export zip (the database, settings, file changes and a manifest) into a
folder, never over another file.
Makes a backup now, checked like the nightly ones (and kept apart from them).

Puts an export's records in place as the engine starts again, the way a backup is
restored: the app starts it again right after asking.
Restores a backup as the engine starts again: the app starts it again right after.

get.description: What Maku settled as it started again after closing unexpectedly, while it's news.

post.description: The owner has seen it: Home doesn't tell it again.

get.description:
Whether Maku's records are damaged, and what can bring them back; null while they're
fine.

post.description:
Restores the newest backup that opens over the damaged records, which are kept beside it
as they are. The app starts the engine again right after.

Sets the damaged records aside as they are, so Maku starts again with new ones, as on its
first day. The app starts the engine again right after.

get.description:
The open video from `at` seconds, as fragmented MP4 the window plays as it comes: the
`sound` track in stereo, and the `subtitles` drawn in once they're ready. The ticket is the
key: no token. A new stream of the same video stops this one.
